247	    def initialize(self) -> None:
248	        # The empty-manifest decision is made under the workspace lock so a
249	        # concurrent first import cannot have its sample replaced by an empty
250	        # dataset created from a stale "manifest missing" observation.
251	        with self._locked(create=True):
252	            if not self.manifest_path.exists():
253	                self._write_json_atomic(
254	                    self.manifest_path, {"schema_version": 1, "items": []}
255	                )
256	            else:
257	                # An existing manifest is never rebuilt, emptied or
258	                # normalized away — but initializing over a structurally
259	                # broken one must not report success, so the corruption is
260	                # surfaced here exactly as for any other operation.
261	                self._read()
262	
263	    def add(self, source: Path, label: str | None = None) -> ImportResult:
264	        # The label is validated before anything else — before the source
265	        # is even looked at — so an illegal label fails this call outright
266	        # and can never reach the manifest, not even on a re-import of
267	        # already registered content (which would otherwise report a
268	        # harmless "already present" success).
269	        _validate_import_label(label)
270	        self.initialize()
271	        file_path = source.resolve(strict=True)
272	        if not file_path.is_file():
273	            raise ValueError(f"Not a regular file: {source}")
274	        # Hashing is pure I/O on the source file; do it before taking the
275	        # workspace lock so concurrent imports of different files hash in
276	        # parallel and only serialize for the manifest check-and-commit.
277	        # The digest and the size must describe one stable file: the read
278	        # fails if the file's identity, size or modification time changes
279	        # around or during the read, so a source being rewritten or
280	        # replaced is rejected instead of registering a digest/size pair
281	        # that never coexisted.
282	        digest, size = self._read_stable(file_path, str(file_path))
283	        with self._locked(create=True):
284	            manifest = self._read()
285	            if any(item["sha256"] == digest for item in manifest["items"]):
286	                # Re-import never overwrites the registered source, label or
287	                # revision: the first report of a digest owns its metadata.
288	                return ImportResult(digest=digest, added=False)
289	            manifest["items"].append(
290	                {
291	                    "sha256": digest,
292	                    "source": str(file_path),
293	                    "size": size,
294	                    "label": label,
295	                }
296	            )
297	            manifest["items"].sort(key=lambda item: item["sha256"])
298	            # Commit through the same journal as batches so the import is
299	            # crash-safe and cannot clobber a batch committed concurrently.
300	            self._commit(manifest, self._read_history())
301	            return ImportResult(digest=digest, added=True)
302	
303	    def import_directory(
304	        self, source: Path, label: str | None = None, recursive: bool = False
305	    ) -> dict[str, Any]:
306	        """Import every accepted image file under a source directory at once.
307	
308	        Candidates are regular files (never symlinks or other entry types)
309	        whose lower-cased extension is one of :data:`IMAGE_EXTENSIONS`;
310	        recursion stays on the top level unless ``recursive`` is set and
311	        never descends through symlinked directories.  They are ordered by
312	        path relative to the source directory, with ``/`` separators,
313	        compared by Unicode code point.
314	
315	        Every candidate is read in full and identified by its full
316	        SHA-256 digest.  A digest already in the workspace, or first seen
317	        on an earlier candidate in this same import, is reported as a
318	        duplicate: the earliest sorted candidate owns the registration and
319	        later paths never overwrite its source or label.  The supplied
320	        label is attached only to genuinely new samples; ``None`` and the
321	        empty string both mean unlabeled.
322	
323	        The whole batch commits as one journal transaction.  The import
324	        fails entirely (no new samples) when the label is not a string or
325	        ``None``, when the source is missing or not a directory, a
326	        directory that should be visited cannot be scanned,
327	        a candidate cannot be read in full, a candidate's identity,
328	        size or modification time changes while it is being read, or a
329	        subdirectory confirmed as a real directory is replaced by a
330	        symbolic link before its scan or before its candidates finish
331	        reading — the link target's images are never imported or even
332	        reported as duplicates.  The label check comes first of all, so
333	        an illegal label fails the call even when the directory is empty
334	        or every candidate is already registered.
335	        """
336	        _validate_import_label(label)
337	        self.initialize()
338	        source_path = Path(source)
339	        if not source_path.exists():
340	            raise ValueError(f"source directory does not exist: {source}")
341	        if not source_path.is_dir():
342	            raise ValueError(f"source is not a directory: {source}")
343	        root = source_path.resolve()
344	
345	        rel_paths, confirmed_dirs = self._scan_image_files(root, recursive)
346	        # Read (and re-stat) every candidate before taking the workspace
347	        # lock: I/O overlaps with peers, and a file that changes mid-read
348	        # fails the whole batch before anything is committed.  A confirmed
349	        # subdirectory swapped for a symlink is never read through: every
350	        # candidate's ancestor directories are re-checked before it is
351	        # opened, the open itself is pinned to the confirmed ancestor
352	        # directories with O_NOFOLLOW descriptors, and the confirmed
353	        # directories are checked once more after all reads, so the link
354	        # target's images cannot be imported or even reported as
355	        # duplicates.
356	        candidates = []
357	        for rel_path in rel_paths:
358	            ancestor = root
359	            for part in Path(rel_path).parts[:-1]:
360	                ancestor = ancestor / part
361	                self._raise_if_now_symlink(ancestor)
362	            candidates.append(self._read_candidate(root / rel_path, rel_path))
363	        for directory in confirmed_dirs:
364	            self._raise_if_now_symlink(directory)
365	
366	        with self._locked(create=True):
367	            manifest = self._read()
368	            history = self._read_history()
369	            known = {item["sha256"] for item in manifest["items"]}
370	
371	            results: list[dict[str, Any]] = []
372	            new_items: list[dict[str, Any]] = []
373	            for rel_path, abs_path, digest, size in candidates:
374	                if digest in known:
375	                    status = "duplicate"
376	                else:
377	                    status = "added"
378	                    known.add(digest)
379	                    new_items.append(
380	                        {
381	                            "sha256": digest,
382	                            "source": str(abs_path.resolve()),
383	                            "size": size,
384	                            "label": label,
385	                        }
386	                    )
387	                results.append(
388	                    {"path": rel_path, "sha256": digest, "status": status}
389	                )
390	
391	            if new_items:
392	                manifest["items"].extend(new_items)
393	                manifest["items"].sort(key=lambda item: item["sha256"])
394	                # One journal commit for the whole batch: an interruption
395	                # leaves either the old state or every new sample together.
396	                self._commit(manifest, history)
397	
398	        added = sum(1 for result in results if result["status"] == "added")
399	        duplicates = len(results) - added
400	        return {
401	            "directory": str(root),
402	            "recursive": recursive,
403	            "label": label,
404	            "candidate_count": len(results),
405	            "added": added,
406	            "duplicates": duplicates,
407	            "candidates": results,
408	        }

410	    def _scan_image_files(
411	        self, root: Path, recursive: bool
412	    ) -> tuple[list[str], list[Path]]:
413	        """Return accepted files and the real directories descended into.
414	
415	        The first element lists accepted files as ``/``-separated paths
416	        relative to root; the second lists every subdirectory confirmed as
417	        a real directory and descended into (empty unless ``recursive``).
418	
419	        Only real regular files qualify; symlinks and other entry types are
420	        skipped, and recursion never follows symlinked directories.  Any
421	        directory that should be visited but cannot be scanned fails the
422	        whole import with the path and reason.  Every confirmed
423	        subdirectory is opened through its pinned parent directory with
424	        ``O_DIRECTORY | O_NOFOLLOW`` and scanned through that descriptor,
425	        so a subdirectory replaced by a symbolic link at any moment before
426	        or during its scan fails the whole import instead of the link
427	        target being scanned.  The confirmed list lets the caller
428	        re-verify the directories once more after the candidate reads.
429	
430	        The descent runs on an explicit stack rather than Python calls:
431	        a tree deeper than the interpreter's recursion limit is scanned in
432	        full instead of aborting partway with a ``RecursionError``, and a
433	        confirmed directory's descriptor stays open for exactly as long as
434	        its subtree is being visited, just as with the former recursive
435	        walk.
436	        """
437	        rel_paths: list[str] = []
438	        confirmed_dirs: list[Path] = []
439	
440	        def classify(directory: Path, fd_or_path: Any) -> list[tuple[str, bool, bool]]:
441	            try:
442	                entries = list(os.scandir(fd_or_path))
443	            except OSError as error:
444	                raise ValueError(
445	                    f"cannot scan directory {directory}: {error}"
446	                ) from error
447	            found: list[tuple[str, bool, bool]] = []
448	            for entry in entries:
449	                try:
450	                    is_file = entry.is_file(follow_symlinks=False)
451	                    is_dir = (
452	                        not is_file
453	                        and recursive
454	                        and entry.is_dir(follow_symlinks=False)
455	                    )
456	                except OSError as error:
457	                    raise ValueError(
458	                        f"cannot inspect entry {directory / entry.name}: {error}"
459	                    ) from error
460	                found.append((entry.name, is_file, is_dir))
461	            return found
462	
463	        try:
464	            root_fd = self._open_real_directory(str(root), None, root)
465	        except OSError as error:
466	            raise ValueError(f"cannot scan directory {root}: {error}") from error
467	
468	        # A frame is one entered directory: its pinned descriptor, its
469	        # path, its slash-relative prefix and the entries still to visit
470	        # (reversed, so pop() yields scan order).  The frame list is the
471	        # iterative counterpart of the recursive call chain: a parent
472	        # frame — with its descriptor still open — stays on the stack for
473	        # the whole time its subtree is processed, at every depth.
474	        frames: list[tuple[int, Path, str, list[tuple[str, bool, bool]]]] = []
475	        try:
476	            # The root is listed by its path; every descendant is listed
477	            # through its pinned descriptor.  root_fd still anchors the
478	            # no-follow open of the root's own children.
479	            frames.append(
480	                (root_fd, root, "", list(reversed(classify(root, root))))
481	            )
482	            while frames:
483	                parent_fd, directory, rel_prefix, entries = frames[-1]
484	                if not entries:
485	                    frames.pop()
486	                    if parent_fd != root_fd:
487	                        os.close(parent_fd)
488	                    continue
489	                name, is_file, is_dir = entries.pop()
490	                if is_file:
491	                    if Path(name).suffix.lower() in IMAGE_EXTENSIONS:
492	                        rel_paths.append(rel_prefix + name)
493	                elif is_dir:
494	                    subdirectory = directory / name
495	                    # Open the confirmed subdirectory through the pinned
496	                    # parent with O_NOFOLLOW and scan the descriptor
497	                    # itself: a symlink swapped onto the path by now fails
498	                    # the whole import here, and the link target is never
499	                    # scanned.
500	                    try:
501	                        child_fd = self._open_real_directory(
502	                            name, parent_fd, subdirectory
503	                        )
504	                    except OSError as error:
505	                        raise ValueError(
506	                            f"cannot scan directory {subdirectory}: {error}"
507	                        ) from error
508	                    transferred = False
509	                    try:
510	                        child_entries = classify(subdirectory, child_fd)
511	                        confirmed_dirs.append(subdirectory)
512	                        frames.append(
513	                            (
514	                                child_fd,
515	                                subdirectory,
516	                                rel_prefix + name + "/",
517	                                list(reversed(child_entries)),
518	                            )
519	                        )
520	                        # The descriptor now belongs to the frame and is
521	                        # closed when that frame finishes; the finally must
522	                        # not close it on the successful path.
523	                        transferred = True
524	                    finally:
525	                        if not transferred:
526	                            os.close(child_fd)
527	        finally:
528	            # On an error mid-walk, close every confirmed descendant
529	            # descriptor still held by an unfinished frame; the root
530	            # descriptor itself is always closed here.
531	            for descriptor, *_ in frames:
532	                if descriptor != root_fd:
533	                    os.close(descriptor)
534	            os.close(root_fd)
535	        # Unicode code point order on the slash-separated relative path.
536	        rel_paths.sort()
537	        return rel_paths, confirmed_dirs
538	
539	    @staticmethod
540	    def _open_real_directory(name: str, dir_fd: int | None, path: Path) -> int:
541	        """Open a confirmed directory, refusing a symlink swapped onto it.
542	
543	        The open uses ``O_DIRECTORY | O_NOFOLLOW`` — relative to the
544	        pinned parent descriptor when ``dir_fd`` is given — so a symbolic
545	        link (or any non-directory) that replaced the confirmed directory
546	        is never descended through.  A symlink swap raises the import's
547	        "directory changed" error naming the replaced path; any other
548	        open failure propagates as the underlying :class:`OSError`.
549	        """
550	        try:
551	            return os.open(name, _DIRECTORY_OPEN_FLAGS, dir_fd=dir_fd)
552	        except OSError as error:
553	            # Linux reports a symlink opened with O_NOFOLLOW|O_DIRECTORY
554	            # as ENOTDIR rather than ELOOP, so confirm via lstat() either
555	            # way.
556	            if error.errno in (errno.ELOOP, errno.ENOTDIR):
557	                try:
558	                    current = os.lstat(path)
559	                except OSError:
560	                    current = None
561	                if current is not None and stat.S_ISLNK(current.st_mode):
562	                    raise ValueError(
563	                        f"directory changed during import: {path} "
564	                        "is now a symbolic link"
565	                    ) from error
566	            raise
567	
568	    @staticmethod
569	    def _raise_if_now_symlink(directory: Path) -> None:
570	        """Fail if a previously confirmed real directory is now a symlink.
571	
572	        A path that vanished is left to the candidate reads (or ignored
573	        when the directory held no candidates); only the symlink swap is
574	        rejected here, because following the link would import the target's
575	        images against the no-symlinked-directories rule.
576	        """
577	        try:
578	            current = os.lstat(directory)
579	        except OSError:
580	            return
581	        if stat.S_ISLNK(current.st_mode):
582	            raise ValueError(
583	                f"directory changed during import: {directory} "
584	                "is now a symbolic link"
585	            )
586	
587	    def _read_candidate(
588	        self, path: Path, rel_path: str
589	    ) -> tuple[str, Path, str, int]:
590	        """Read one candidate in full, verifying identity/size/mtime around it.
591	
592	        Returns ``(rel_path, absolute_path, digest, size)``.  A mismatch or
593	        read failure raises before the batch is committed.
594	
595	        Every ancestor directory of the candidate is re-opened from the
596	        source root with ``O_DIRECTORY | O_NOFOLLOW``, each relative to its
597	        pinned parent, and the candidate itself is opened relative to its
598	        pinned parent directory: a subdirectory replaced by a symbolic
599	        link since the scan fails the whole import here, and the link
600	        target's images are never opened — no matter when the swap lands.
601	        """
602	        parts = Path(rel_path).parts
603	        root = path
604	        for _ in parts:
605	            root = root.parent
606	        try:
607	            fd = self._open_real_directory(str(root), None, root)
608	        except OSError as error:
609	            raise ValueError(f"cannot read {rel_path}: {error}") from error
610	        try:
611	            ancestor = root
612	            for part in parts[:-1]:
613	                ancestor = ancestor / part
614	                try:
615	                    next_fd = self._open_real_directory(part, fd, ancestor)
616	                except OSError as error:
617	                    raise ValueError(
618	                        f"cannot read {rel_path}: {error}"
619	                    ) from error
620	                os.close(fd)
621	                fd = next_fd
622	            digest, size = self._read_stable(
623	                path, rel_path, dir_fd=fd, name=parts[-1]
624	            )
625	        finally:
626	            os.close(fd)
627	        return rel_path, path, digest, size

629	    @staticmethod
630	    def _read_stable(
631	        path: Path,
632	        display: str,
633	        *,
634	        dir_fd: int | None = None,
635	        name: str | None = None,
636	    ) -> tuple[str, int]:
637	        """Read one file in full and return ``(digest, size)`` for it.
638	
639	        The digest and size are guaranteed to describe the same stable
640	        regular file: the path is lstat()ed without following symlinks
641	        and opened with ``O_NOFOLLOW``, the opened descriptor is
642	        fstat()ed to prove it is the inode that was confirmed, and the
643	        path is lstat()ed again after the read, requiring the same
644	        object with the same size and modification time.  Any identity,
645	        size or modification-time change — in-place rewrites, appends,
646	        truncation, delete-and-recreate, or replacing the path with
647	        another file, even one with identical content, size and mtime —
648	        fails with the path and reason, as do a vanishing path, a
649	        non-regular file and any open or read error.
650	
651	        The confirm/open/prove rule itself lives in :mod:`confirmed`
652	        and is shared with the source-directory export; only the
653	        post-read stability requirement and the import wording are
654	        specific to this entry point.
655	
656	        When ``dir_fd`` and ``name`` are given (whole-directory import),
657	        the pre-open inspection and the post-read re-inspection stay on
658	        the path, but the open itself is ``name`` relative to the pinned
659	        parent directory descriptor: an ancestor directory replaced by a
660	        symbolic link can never redirect the open into the link target.
661	        """
662	        try:
663	            if dir_fd is None:
664	                opened_file = confirmed.confirm_and_open_regular(path)
665	            else:
666	                confirmed_status = confirmed.inspect_regular(path)
667	                descriptor = confirmed.open_without_follow(name, dir_fd=dir_fd)
668	                opened_file = confirmed.ConfirmedOpen(
669	                    descriptor,
670	                    confirmed_status,
671	                    confirmed.prove_opened_regular(descriptor, confirmed_status),
672	                )
673	        except confirmed.ConfirmationError as failure:
674	            raise _import_confirmation_error(failure, display) from failure
675	        try:
676	            digest = confirmed.hash_descriptor(opened_file.descriptor)
677	        except OSError as error:
678	            raise ValueError(f"cannot read {display}: {error}") from error
679	        # Import, unlike export, also requires the path itself to still
680	        # name the same unchanged file after the read: an in-place
681	        # rewrite, append, truncation or replacement that landed while
682	        # the bytes were streamed must not register a digest/size pair
683	        # that never coexisted.
684	        try:
685	            after = os.lstat(path)
686	        except OSError as error:
687	            raise ValueError(f"cannot read {display}: {error}") from error
688	        if not confirmed.same_identity_size_mtime(opened_file.confirmed, after):
689	            raise ValueError(
690	                f"file changed during import: {display} "
691	                "(identity, size or modification time changed)"
692	            )
693	        return digest, opened_file.confirmed.st_size

706	    def find_by_label(self, label: str) -> dict[str, Any]:
707	        """List samples currently registered under one exact category label.
708	
709	        Matching is exact on the current manifest label: case, surrounding
710	        whitespace and path separators are all kept literally, so ``"cat"``
711	        never matches ``"Cat"`` or ``"cat "``.  The empty string queries
712	        unlabeled samples — records whose stored label is ``None`` or ``""``
713	        — and every matching record's label is reported uniformly as
714	        ``None``.  A genuine class literally named ``"unlabeled"`` is
715	        queried with that text and never mixed with unlabeled samples,
716	        unlike :meth:`summary` which merges them under one display key.
717	
718	        Each record provides the full SHA-256 digest, the source path saved
719	        at first registration, the byte size and the current label;
720	        records are sorted ascending by full digest and ``count`` always
721	        equals the list length.  The query reads the registered records
722	        only — it never opens a source file, and saved split plans' old
723	        labels are neither matched nor rewritten — so a moved, deleted or
724	        unreadable source is still found, and a batch update or undo
725	        committed before the call is immediately reflected.
726	        """
727	        if not isinstance(label, str):
728	            raise BatchError("query label must be a string")
729	        want_unlabeled = label == ""
730	        samples: list[dict[str, Any]] = []
731	        self.initialize()
732	        with self._locked():
733	            items = self._read()["items"]
734	        for item in items:
735	            stored = item.get("label")
736	            if want_unlabeled:
737	                if not (stored is None or stored == ""):
738	                    continue
739	                current = None
740	            else:
741	                if stored != label:
742	                    continue
743	                current = stored
744	            samples.append(
745	                {
746	                    "sha256": item["sha256"],
747	                    "source": item["source"],
748	                    "size": item["size"],
749	                    "label": current,
750	                }
751	            )
752	        samples.sort(key=lambda sample: sample["sha256"])
753	        return {"label": label, "count": len(samples), "samples": samples}

779	    def submit_batch(self, data: Any) -> dict[str, Any]:
780	        """Validate and apply a batch label update.
781	
782	        Parsing happens before the lock; inside the lock the submission
783	        runs through clearly separated stages, each with one job:
784	
785	        1. **Unknown samples** — every named digest must be registered; the
786	           first unknown one rejects the batch with nothing written.
787	        2. **Number identity** — the submitted number must identify at
788	           most one entry in the full history list.  A second entry
789	           carrying that same number, whether adjacent to the first or
790	           separated by other batches, is refused outright as damaged
791	           history: identical content, different samples, different
792	           changes or an already-undone first occurrence never select a
793	           winner.  The unique matching history batch is then itself
794	           refused when damaged: it may list each sample at most once (a
795	           repeated full SHA-256 digest, however the copies differ, is
796	           corruption), every one of its records must explicitly save
797	           both the before (``old``) and after (``new``) label (an
798	           explicit ``null``/``""`` counts as saved), and each record's
799	           ``changed`` flag must agree with those saved labels (differing
800	           labels require ``true``, identical labels require ``false``,
801	           judged from the history row alone).  These refusals
802	           come before either verdict below.  An intact known number
803	           then replays the first submission's result (same content) or
804	           conflicts (different content); neither touches the manifest.
805	        3. **Verification/classification** — each current label is read
806	           once: an expected-old mismatch rejects the batch, and the same
807	           reading decides whether that record actually changes.
808	        4. **Application** — only records classified as changed are
809	           mutated; if none are, the batch occupies no number and writes
810	           no history.
811	        5. **History and save** — the entry and result are assembled from
812	           the applied records, and manifest plus history commit together
813	           through the journal.
814	
815	        No stage mutates anything before every earlier stage has passed, so
816	        a rejection can neither leave partially updated samples nor a
817	        partial history entry.
818	        """
819	        number, records = parse_batch_file(data)
820	        with self._locked(create=True):
821	            manifest = self._read()
822	            history = self._read_history()
823	            items = {item["sha256"]: item for item in manifest["items"]}
824	
825	            # Stage 1: every record must name a registered sample.
826	            reject_unknown_samples(records, items.__contains__)
827	
828	            # Stage 2: a known number is replayed or conflicts; a fresh
829	            # number proceeds without examining the current labels.
830	            # require_unique_history_number first refuses a number that
831	            # occurs on at least two entries anywhere in the full history
832	            # list — adjacent or separated by other batches, identical or
833	            # different, already undone or not — before this submission
834	            # could be matched against a first or active entry.  Only a
835	            # unique same-number entry is then handed to
836	            # resolve_re_submission, which refuses a damaged one (a
837	            # repeated sample digest, a record missing its saved
838	            # old/new label, or a changed flag contradicting those
839	            # labels) before it can compare or replay anything.
840	            require_unique_history_number(number, history["batches"])
841	            existing = next(
842	                (entry for entry in history["batches"] if entry["batch"] == number),
843	                None,
844	            )
845	            replay = resolve_re_submission(number, records, existing)
846	            if replay is not None:
847	                return replay
848	
849	            # Stage 3: verify expected old labels and classify changed vs
850	            # unchanged in a single current-label pass.
851	            resolutions = verify_records(
852	                records,
853	                lambda digest: normalize_label(items[digest].get("label")),
854	            )
855	
856	            # Stage 4: apply is the only mutation.  No changes at all
857	            # occupies no batch number and writes no history.
858	            if not any(resolution.changed for resolution in resolutions):
859	                return no_changes_result(number, len(records))
860	            applied_records = apply_resolutions(resolutions, items)
861	
862	            # Stage 5: assemble history, then save manifest and history
863	            # together through the journal.
864	            entry = build_history_entry(number, applied_records)
865	            history["batches"].append(entry)
866	            self._commit(manifest, history)
867	            return result_payload(number, "applied", applied_records)
868	
869	    def undo_batch(self, number: str) -> dict[str, Any]:
870	        """Undo a successful batch by number.
871	
872	        Only samples the batch actually changed are checked: each must have
873	        the same label revision it had right after the batch (no later
874	        modification, even one that restored the same label).  Repeated
875	        undos are idempotent and do not add history.
876	
877	        Integrity comes before either verdict.  First the requested number
878	        must identify exactly one entry in the saved batch list: a second
879	        entry carrying that same number — identical content or different,
880	        adjacent or separated by other batches, already undone or not — is
881	        batch history corruption, never a first-match/last-match/active
882	        choice and never a merge.  The target batch must then name every
883	        sample with a well-formed identity (exactly 64 lowercase
884	        hexadecimal characters), list every sample exactly once, carry a
885	        sound pinned revision on each record, explicitly save both
886	        before/after labels on each record, and have every record's
887	        ``changed`` flag agree with the before/after labels saved on that
888	        same record.  A duplicated number, a malformed ``sha256`` value,
889	        a duplicated digest, a bad row, a missing label field or a flag
890	        that contradicts its labels rejects the undo even when the batch
891	        is already marked undone, so corruption is never hidden behind an
892	        ``already-undone`` success or confused with a sample modified
893	        after the batch.
894	        """
895	        with self._locked(create=True):
896	            manifest = self._read()
897	            history = self._read_history()
898	            entry = find_unique_history_entry(number, history["batches"])
899	            if entry is None:
900	                raise BatchError(f"unknown batch number: {number!r}")
901	
902	            # find_unique_history_entry scans the whole list, so a second
903	            # same-number entry — adjacent or behind other batches,
904	            # identical content or different, already undone or active —
905	            # raises before this point; repeats of other numbers do not
906	            # match and stay irrelevant.
907	            #
908	            # Validate the unique target batch's integrity — every row's
909	            # sha256 in registered-identity format, one row per sample,
910	            # sound pinned revisions, both before/after labels saved, and a
911	            # changed flag that matches those labels — before the
912	            # already-undone short-circuit and the later-modification
913	            # checks: a malformed, duplicated, inconsistent or corrupt
914	            # history record is refusal, not an undo, a no-op or an
915	            # unknown batch, and nothing is rewritten.  Identity format
916	            # is judged first: a bad spelling on an unchanged row, or on
917	            # a row behind restorable ones, must still fail the whole
918	            # undo before anything is restored.
919	            require_intact_history_digests(entry)
920	            require_intact_history_records(entry)
921	            require_intact_history_revisions(entry)
922	            require_intact_history_labels(entry)
923	            require_intact_history_changes(entry)
924	
925	            if entry["undone"]:
926	                return {"batch": number, "status": "already-undone", "restored": 0}
927	
928	            items = {item["sha256"]: item for item in manifest["items"]}
929	            for record in entry["records"]:
930	                if not record["changed"]:
931	                    continue
932	                item = items.get(record["sha256"])
933	                if item is None:
934	                    raise BatchError(
935	                        f"cannot undo batch {number!r}: sample {record['sha256']} "
936	                        "is no longer in the manifest"
937	                    )
938	                current = normalize_label(item.get("label"))
939	                # record["rev"] is now known to be a genuine non-negative
940	                # integer, so a boolean/decimal/string can never compare
941	                # equal to the sample's current revision.  The stored
942	                # after-label is normalized before comparing: history may
943	                # explicitly save either unlabeled spelling (null or ""),
944	                # and both match a sample currently unlabeled either way.
945	                if item_revision(item) != record["rev"] or current != normalize_label(
946	                    record["new"]
947	                ):
948	                    raise BatchError(
949	                        f"cannot undo batch {number!r}: sample {record['sha256']} "
950	                        "was modified after the batch"
951	                    )
952	
953	            restored = 0
954	            for record in entry["records"]:
955	                if not record["changed"]:
956	                    continue
957	                item = items[record["sha256"]]
958	                item["label"] = record["old"]
959	                item["rev"] = item_revision(item) + 1
960	                restored += 1
961	
962	            entry["undone"] = True
963	            entry["undone_at"] = datetime.now(timezone.utc).isoformat()
964	            self._commit(manifest, history)
965	            return {"batch": number, "status": "undone", "restored": restored}

976	    @contextmanager
977	    def _workspace_lock(self):
978	        """Exclusive workspace lock for check-and-write transactions.
979	
980	        ``flock`` is advisory but sufficient for local processes: holders
981	        serialize, so every read-modify-write observes the state left by the
982	        previous completed operation.
983	        """
984	        self.state_directory.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
985	        descriptor = os.open(self.lock_path, os.O_RDWR | os.O_CREAT, 0o600)
986	        try:
987	            fcntl.flock(descriptor, fcntl.LOCK_EX)
988	            yield
989	        finally:
990	            try:
991	                fcntl.flock(descriptor, fcntl.LOCK_UN)
992	            finally:
993	                os.close(descriptor)

995	    @contextmanager
996	    def _locked(self, *, create: bool = False):
997	        """Hold the workspace lock and finish any leftover prepared journal.
998	
999	        Recovery runs once the lock is held, so a long-lived process that
1000	        only imports, queries or creates plans still installs the prepared
1001	        transaction of a process that crashed on this machine, without
1002	        needing to reopen the workspace.
1003	
1004	        Read callers leave ``create`` false: on a workspace whose state
1005	        directory does not yet exist there is no journal to finish and
1006	        nothing for a writer to hold, so the query proceeds (and fails or
1007	        reports empty exactly as before) without materializing one.
1008	        """
1009	        if not create and not self.state_directory.exists():
1010	            yield
1011	            return
1012	        with self._workspace_lock():
1013	            self._recover_transaction_locked()
1014	            yield
1015	
1016	    def _recover_if_needed(self) -> None:
1017	        """Finish a prepared transaction left by a crashed process."""
1018	        if not self.transaction_path.exists():
1019	            return
1020	        with self._locked():
1021	            pass
1022	
1023	    def _recover_transaction_locked(self) -> None:
1024	        if not self.transaction_path.exists():
1025	            return
1026	        try:
1027	            journal = json.loads(self.transaction_path.read_text(encoding="utf-8"))
1028	        except (OSError, json.JSONDecodeError) as error:
1029	            raise BatchError(f"cannot recover interrupted transaction: {error}") from error
1030	        manifest = journal.get("manifest")
1031	        history = journal.get("batches")
1032	        if not isinstance(history, dict):
1033	            raise BatchError("cannot recover interrupted transaction: journal is malformed")
1034	        # Only install a coherent, fully valid pair, so recovery can never
1035	        # replace the committed manifest with a structurally broken sample
1036	        # list (a missing field, a bad field type or a duplicated digest):
1037	        # the check runs before either file is rewritten, leaving both the
1038	        # last committed registration and its history untouched.
1039	        try:
1040	            validate_manifest(manifest)
1041	        except ManifestError as error:
1042	            raise BatchError(
1043	                f"cannot recover interrupted transaction: {error}"
1044	            ) from error
1045	        validate_history(history)
1046	        # Idempotent installs: both files end up at the journal's version.
1047	        self._write_json_atomic(self.manifest_path, manifest)
1048	        self._write_json_atomic(self.batches_path, history)
1049	        try:
1050	            self.transaction_path.unlink()
1051	        except OSError:
1052	            pass
1053	
1054	    def _commit(self, manifest: dict[str, Any], history: dict[str, Any]) -> None:
1055	        """Atomically install the new manifest and history together.
1056	
1057	        A write-ahead journal holding both full payloads is written and
1058	        fsynced first; a crash at any point leaves enough to redo the
1059	        missing install on the next open, so the two files never disagree.
1060	        """
1061	        journal = {"manifest": manifest, "batches": history}
1062	        self._write_json_atomic(self.transaction_path, journal)
1063	        self._write_json_atomic(self.manifest_path, manifest)
1064	        self._write_json_atomic(self.batches_path, history)
1065	        try:
1066	            self.transaction_path.unlink()
1067	        except OSError:
1068	            pass

1070	    def _read_history(self) -> dict[str, Any]:
1071	        if not self.batches_path.exists():
1072	            return empty_history()
1073	        try:
1074	            data = json.loads(self.batches_path.read_text(encoding="utf-8"))
1075	        except (OSError, json.JSONDecodeError) as error:
1076	            raise BatchError(f"cannot read batch history: {error}") from error
1077	        return validate_history(data)

1083	    def create_split(
1084	        self, name: str, seed: int, ratios: list[float | int | str | Fraction]
1085	    ) -> SplitPlanResult:
1086	        """Create (or reuse) a named train/validation/test plan.
1087	
1088	        The plan snapshots every sample currently in the manifest.  A
1089	        second call with the same name returns the stored plan unchanged
1090	        when the inputs match; otherwise it reports a name conflict.
1091	        """
1092	        validate_name(name)
1093	        if isinstance(seed, bool) or not isinstance(seed, int):
1094	            raise SplitError(f"Seed must be an integer, got {seed!r}")
1095	        fraction_ratios = validate_ratios(ratios)
1096	
1097	        self.initialize()
1098	        plan_path = self._split_path(name)
1099	
1100	        with self._locked(create=True):
1101	            # Sample identities and labels are read from one complete
1102	            # manifest state, so a batch committing concurrently is observed
1103	            # either entirely (all its label changes) or not at all.
1104	            items = self._read()["items"]
1105	            # assign() validates identities and performs the stratification.
1106	            assignment = assign(items, fraction_ratios, seed)
1107	
1108	            snapshot = [
1109	                {
1110	                    "sha256": item["sha256"],
1111	                    "label": item.get("label"),
1112	                    "source": item.get("source"),
1113	                }
1114	                for item in sorted(items, key=lambda item: item["sha256"])
1115	            ]
1116	            plan_payload = self._build_plan(
1117	                name, seed, fraction_ratios, snapshot, assignment
1118	            )
1119	
1120	            # The check-and-create is atomic under the same lock, so among
1121	            # concurrent creations of one name exactly one reports success;
1122	            # matching requests reuse it and differing ones conflict.
1123	            if plan_path.exists():
1124	                existing = self._read_split(plan_path)
1125	                if self._same_inputs(existing, seed, fraction_ratios, snapshot):
1126	                    return SplitPlanResult(name=name, created=False, plan=existing)
1127	                raise SplitError(
1128	                    f"Split plan {name!r} already exists with different seed, "
1129	                    "ratios or samples; choose another name"
1130	                )
1131	
1132	            self._write_json_atomic(plan_path, plan_payload)
1133	            return SplitPlanResult(name=name, created=True, plan=plan_payload)

1147	    def _build_plan(
1148	        self,
1149	        name: str,
1150	        seed: int,
1151	        ratios: tuple[Fraction, Fraction, Fraction],
1152	        snapshot: list[dict[str, Any]],
1153	        assignment: dict[str, str],
1154	    ) -> dict[str, Any]:
1155	        sets = {set_name: [] for set_name in SET_NAMES}
1156	        for sample in snapshot:
